title: Staff Personal Data and HR Records Policy
summary: How we collect, use, protect, share and delete personal information about applicants, employees, former employees, Directors, agency workers, students, volunteers and contractors: what the staff record holds and why, who may open its restricted section, how staff see and correct their information, how references and outside requests are answered, what we monitor, and how long staff records are kept. For all employees, with detail for managers and the HR Manager.

keyPoints.intro: We hold your personal information to employ you, pay you, keep you safe and meet the law. These points tell you what to keep up to date, how sensitive information is protected, and how to treat information about colleagues.
points: Never look at a colleague's record unless your work needs it, and never share a colleague's phone number, address, health, absence or circumstances with anyone, including the people we support and their families. This is a disciplinary matter and can be a criminal offence.
If a payslip, letter, email or list with staff details is lost or reaches the wrong person, phone the office or the On-call Manager at once and record it in the incident log before your shift ends.

Never give a reference or confirm anyone's employment for {{organisation}}. Pass every reference request, and any request about a colleague from the police, a lender, a landlord or anyone else, to the HR Manager the same working day.

Give health, criminal record and other sensitive information only to the HR Manager or a manager this policy names. Supervisors and Care Coordinators learn only how it affects your work, unless you agree; for infection symptoms, only the symptom group, dates and restrictions are recorded.

If you supervise or manage staff, record everything about a worker in CareFlow. Never keep notes, files, photographs or messages about staff on paper, a personal phone, personal email or a messaging app.

Tell the HR Manager within 5 working days if your address, phone number, emergency contact or vehicle changes. Bank details change only by email from the address in your staff record or in person with photo ID, and we phone you to confirm.
Texts about your employment only ask you to phone in or arrange a meeting. Health, pay, conduct and immigration matters reach you by encrypted email, letter or in person.

CareFlow records your phone's location only at check-in and check-out, if you leave the home while checked in, or with an emergency alert, never between visits. We never monitor your personal phone or social media.

Ask the HR Manager for your own information. Payslip, contract and rota copies come within 5 working days, other everyday records within 10; a request for everything we hold is answered within one month, free of charge.
Tell the HR Manager if anything we hold about you is wrong; it is corrected within 10 working days. You check your personal details each year at your appraisal.

When you leave, your CareFlow access ends on your last working day and your DBS certificate copy is deleted. Most of your staff record is kept for 6 years after you leave, then deleted except for a short summary.

blocks.p: {{organisation}} holds a great deal of personal information about the people who work for us and apply to us, from identity, criminal record and health information to bank details, home addresses, family circumstances and records of absence, conduct and performance. Staff trust us with it, often at difficult times. Our care workers work alone and travel between people's homes on rotas, so a home address, phone number or rota in the wrong hands can put them at risk.

{{organisation}} is the controller of all staff and applicant information. We collect only what employment, the law and safe care need; keep it in the staff record in CareFlow, with health, criminal record and other sensitive information in a restricted section open only to the managers named in this policy; tell staff how it is used; share it only as this policy allows; keep it accurate; and delete it on time. The law requires us to keep secure records about the people we employ and to have the Schedule 3 information available for each of them (Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014, regulations 17(2)(d) and 19(3)). This policy applies our Data Protection Policy to staff and applicant records.

bullets: Every item of staff and applicant information has a purpose, a lawful basis, a place in the staff record, named people who may see it and a retention period.
Sensitive information is seen only by the managers who need it; supervisors and Care Coordinators learn only what allocation and supervision need.

Staff know what we hold and can see and correct it; references and outside requests are answered by one person, accurately and on time; and the Schedule 3 information is complete for every person employed and can be shown to CQC.

blocks.p: This policy covers personal information about applicants, employees (including bank staff, apprentices and staff on probation, leave or suspension), former employees, Directors, agency workers, students on placement, volunteers and contractors, in any form: CareFlow, email, payroll, paper and phone calls. It applies to everyone who handles that information, and through their contracts to our processors, such as our payroll bureau, pension provider, occupational health provider and DBS umbrella body.

Owned elsewhere: organisation-wide lawful bases, privacy notices and DPIAs (Data Protection Policy); rights request steps (Subject Access and Individual Rights Procedure); breach handling (Personal Data Breach Procedure); the retention schedule and destruction (Records Management and Retention Policy); sharing decisions generally (Confidentiality and Information Sharing Policy); recruitment checks (Safer Recruitment Policy; Pre-Employment Checks and DBS Procedure; Right to Work and Sponsored Workers Policy); work phones (Mobile Phones and Social Media Policy); user accounts and technical security (Information and Cyber Security Policy); allegations (Managing Allegations Against Staff Procedure); and DBS and regulator referrals (Staff Fitness Concerns and DBS Referrals Procedure).

rows: Staff record

The CareFlow record for each employee, Director, agency worker, student, volunteer and contractor: personal details, recruitment and checks, contract and pay information, declarations, case files and correspondence, linked to their training and compliance records, supervision and appraisal records and policy acknowledgements. An applicant's recruitment record becomes part of it on appointment.
Restricted section

The sensitive items listed in this policy, held as documents in the staff record. CareFlow opens staff documents only to roles given the staff document permissions, which we give only to the HR Manager, Registered Manager, Deputy Manager and Nominated Individual. Each of them opens only the items this policy names them for, and CareFlow logs every download. Because CareFlow controls this access by role, an item about one of those managers, such as a grievance or complaint about them, is saved as a password-protected document whose password they are not given.
Criminal offence data

Information about convictions, cautions, offences and alleged offences, including DBS certificates, Update Service results, criminal records declarations, overseas certificates and driving licence endorsements. Special category data is defined in the Data Protection Policy.
Staff record summary
The short record the HR Manager creates when a staff record is closed and keeps until the former employee's 75th birthday, as the Records Management and Retention Policy sets out.

blocks.p: The Directors approve this policy and receive the staff figures in the data protection section of each quarterly governance report. The Nominated Individual, as Senior Information Risk Owner, approves processors of staff information, handles staff rights requests that come from or mainly concern the HR Manager or Registered Manager, decides outside requests about a Director, the Registered Manager, Deputy Manager or HR Manager, approves named staff information for commissioners and signs off the quarterly access review.

The Registered Manager owns this policy, approves every reference before it is sent, checks in the quarterly user access review that only the roles named in this policy hold the staff document permissions and that the CareFlow download log shows no restricted item opened by anyone this policy does not name for it, and covers the HR Manager's duties under this policy when the HR Manager is absent or involved. The Deputy Manager covers the Registered Manager.

The HR Manager is the information asset owner for staff, applicant and Director records. They keep the staff record and file restricted items, issue the applicant and employee privacy notices, handle staff rights requests, references and outside requests about staff, lead on breaches of staff information, run the annual personal details check, and close and delete leavers' records on time.
The Deputy Manager carries out the quarterly staff file audit and the staff record sample in the December records and data protection audit.

subsections.heading: Care Coordinators, Field Care Supervisors and supervising Senior Care Workers

blocks.p: They record supervision, spot checks, appraisals and allocation decisions in CareFlow, use only the information their task needs, and pass sensitive information to the HR Manager as the restricted section rules below set out.

They use a worker's emergency contact, vehicle details and photograph only for the worker's safety under the Lone Working and Staff Personal Safety Policy, never confirm to a caller that someone works for us, and pass any request about a member of staff to the HR Manager the same working day. On-call Managers open cleared to work status, skills and sign-offs, training expiry dates, allocation restrictions and infection-related absence entries only to allocate visits out of hours, and record infection-related absence entries as the restricted section rules set out.

Every employee uses colleagues' information only as their work needs and keeps it confidential during and after employment. Looking up, sharing or keeping staff information without a work reason is handled under the Disciplinary Policy and Procedure and can be an offence under section 170 of the Data Protection Act 2018.

We hold only the information below. Lawful bases follow the Data Protection Policy; where special category or criminal offence data is involved, the condition is shown as well. Every use that relies on legitimate interests has a legitimate interests assessment recorded under the Data Protection Policy before it starts.

blocks.p: We never ask for health information before a job offer (other than adjustments to the recruitment process), nationality or immigration history at interview, personal social media accounts, biometric data, or information about family members beyond an emergency contact and what family leave or pay needs. Employees tell their emergency contact that we hold their details. The appropriate policy document that Schedule 1, paragraph 1 requires is kept by the Nominated Individual under the Data Protection Policy.

Sensitive items are kept only in the restricted section. Items are filed there by the HR Manager, the Registered Manager or Deputy Manager, or by the manager another library document makes responsible for that record, such as an allegation case manager's risk assessment or a pregnancy review by a Field Care Supervisor the worker agreed may know the reason. Anyone else who receives such information, such as a fit note, an occupational health letter, a disclosure in supervision or a DBS letter, passes it to the HR Manager the same working day by hand, encrypted email or a phone call, keeps no copy, and records only that a matter was passed to the HR Manager. Office staff and Care Coordinators never open the restricted section, except that an ID checker sees the right to work check they made. Concerns raised under the Whistleblowing (Speaking Up) Policy are never filed in the staff record; they stay in the speaking-up log.

blocks.p: A manager who needs restricted information for a decision asks the HR Manager, who gives only what that decision needs. Care Coordinators and supervisors are told an adjustment or allocation restriction and its end date, never the condition or reason unless the worker agrees, and rota notes never record it. The one exception is infection: when a worker phones in with symptoms, Office staff record only that the worker is unavailable, and the Care Coordinator (the On-call Manager out of hours) records an infection-related absence entry outside the restricted section, holding the symptom group, dates and any restriction with its end date, which Care Coordinators and On-call Managers need for allocation and linked-case checks under the Staff Infection-Related Illness and Exclusion Policy. Diagnoses and medical evidence stay in the restricted section. The Disclosure and Barring Service's guidance recognises that CQC-registered providers may keep certificate information for inspection. We keep one electronic copy in the restricted section, open only to those named above, make no further copies, and delete it when employment ends, keeping only the details that guidance allows.

sections.heading: The staff record and who sees what

blocks.p: CareFlow is our only place for staff and applicant records. Nobody keeps a separate personnel file, spreadsheet, notebook, email folder, photograph or messaging group about staff. A note made on paper at a meeting is entered in CareFlow within 2 working days and the paper shredded. An email that forms part of a worker's record is saved into the staff record within 1 working day, because mailbox items are deleted automatically after 2 years. Access outside the restricted section follows the role.

blocks.p: The people we support and their representatives learn only a worker's first name, description and what the ID badge shows. A worker's personal phone number, home address and circumstances are never given to them or to colleagues without the worker's agreement; a colleague who needs to reach them is offered a message. A care worker asked during a visit why a regular colleague is away, or for their number, says only that the office arranges cover and will pass on a message, and tells the office. The HR Manager changes a user's CareFlow access the day a change of role takes effect, suspends it the same day as a suspension and ends it on the last working day, as the Information and Cyber Security Policy sets out.

sections.heading: Telling staff and sharing staff information

blocks.p: The HR Manager gives the applicant privacy notice with the application form and the employee privacy notice with the offer letter or before the first shift, and goes through it at organisational induction. Agency workers and students receive the employee privacy notice at local induction. A revised notice reaches staff at least 2 weeks before a change in how we use their information takes effect. The notice names the Data Protection Officer, whom staff may contact directly, and the right to complain to the Information Commission (formerly the ICO).

sections.heading: References and other requests about staff

blocks.p: Only the HR Manager gives references for {{organisation}}. Anyone else asked for a reference, or to confirm someone's employment, passes the request to the HR Manager the same working day and confirms nothing. Staff may give a personal character reference only in their own name, from their own email, saying it is personal and using nothing from our records; a manager asked about someone they manage or managed passes the request to the HR Manager.

steps: The HR Manager checks that the request comes from a genuine organisation, using its published address or phone number, and that the worker named us as a referee or agrees.
The HR Manager drafts the reference from the staff record only, using the content rules below.
The Registered Manager approves it, and the HR Manager sends it from their work email to the verified address within 3 working days of receiving the request, keeping a copy in the staff record.

Where a disciplinary, capability or allegation case is open, the HR Manager tells the requester the reference will follow, takes the employment law adviser's and, for an allegation, the local authority's advice, and sends it once advice is received.

Sickness absence, health or disability, pregnancy or family leave, grievances, discrimination complaints, whistleblowing, informal action, expired warnings, allegations that were unsubstantiated, unfounded, false or malicious or had no case to answer, and opinions the records do not support

blocks.p: We give references under legitimate interests (6(1)(f)); the only sensitive content ever included is a substantiated allegation, shared under Schedule 1, paragraph 18 (safeguarding). No settlement agreement or other term ever limits an accurate reference. References are given in confidence and the Data Protection Act 2018, Schedule 2, paragraph 24 exempts them from the right of access; a worker who asks to see a reference we gave or received is handled under the Subject Access and Individual Rights Procedure, and the exemption is used only with the Nominated Individual's approval on the Data Protection Officer's advice.

blocks.p: We use no CCTV at the branch office, vehicle tracking, body-worn cameras, biometric systems or screen or keystroke monitoring, and never monitor personal phones or social media. No decision about a worker is made solely by automated processing; a manager reviews every CareFlow alert or report first. Another employee's mailbox is opened, and covert monitoring used, only as the Acceptable Use of IT and Devices Policy and the Mobile Phones and Social Media Policy allow. New monitoring needs an approved DPIA and a revised privacy notice first.

sections.heading: Keeping information accurate and staff rights

bullets: Employees tell the HR Manager within 5 working days of a change of address, phone number, emergency contact or vehicle; the HR Manager updates the staff record within 2 working days. A change of name is updated with a new ID badge within 5 working days.

Pay goes only into an account in the worker's own name. Bank details change only on a request from the email address in the staff record or in person at the branch office with photo ID, and the HR Manager phones the worker on their recorded number to confirm before the next payroll. A change requested any other way is refused and treated as possible fraud.

Before each annual appraisal the HR Manager sends the employee a summary of their personal details, emergency contact, vehicle, qualifications and document expiry dates; the employee confirms or corrects it at the appraisal.

Gaps or errors in a staff record are corrected within 10 working days by a dated correcting entry, without deleting the original. A worker who disagrees with an opinion recorded about them, such as in a supervision record, has their comments added beside it.

blocks.p: Employees see their rota, visit records and policy acknowledgements in CareFlow. Copies of a payslip, contract or rota are given within 5 working days; a training record, vaccination record, or hours, pay and leave records within 10 working days. A request for more, in any words and to anyone, is passed to the office the same working day and handled by the HR Manager under the Subject Access and Individual Rights Procedure: free of charge, after a reasonable and proportionate search, and answered within one month. While an allegation case, or a police or local authority enquiry into a fitness concern, about the worker is open, the HR Manager checks with the local authority and police before releasing anything, including to the worker. Former employees and applicants have the same rights.

Staff records cannot be erased while we must keep them; we explain why and record the worker's view. Equality monitoring answers are removed within 5 working days of a request. An objection to processing under legitimate interests is decided by the HR Manager on the Data Protection Officer's advice within one month, with the Nominated Individual approving any decision to continue; check-in/check-out and lone worker monitoring continue where safety needs them, and we explain why. A complaint about how we use staff information is handled under the Complaints Policy and Procedure as a High complaint, and the reply tells the worker they may complain to the Information Commission.

bullets: Paper: staff and applicant documents received on paper are kept in the locked HR cabinet in the branch office until the HR Manager scans them, within 2 working days, then shredded. We never keep anyone's original identity documents or passport. Paper kept in a person's home never holds staff contact details or rotas.

Email: HR correspondence is sent only by the HR Manager and managers from work accounts, to the address recorded in the staff record, confirmed by phone before first use. Anything containing health, criminal record, conduct, capability, grievance, allegation, immigration or bank information is sent as an encrypted attachment with the password given separately by phone, or handed over in person in a sealed envelope. Subject lines never pair a name with the matter.

Texts and messaging: messages to staff, including to work phones, only arrange a call or meeting and never contain health, pay, conduct or immigration details. Nobody uses a messaging app for HR matters.
Post: letters are marked private and confidential, addressee only; formal outcome letters go by encrypted email or by a signed-for postal service.

Conversations: staff matters are discussed only in private, at the branch office, by phone or by video, never in a person's home, in a car with others or where they can be overheard; spot check feedback is given away from the person and their family. On-call Managers working from home open staff details only on the on-call laptop or work phone, out of others' sight and hearing. HR documents are printed only at the branch office and collected at once.

steps: On the last working day, the HR Manager ends the worker's CareFlow access and the work phone, ID badge, keys and any papers are returned, as the Mobile Phones and Social Media Policy and the Uniform, ID Badges and Dress Code Policy set out.

Within 1 working day of employment ending, the HR Manager deletes the DBS certificate copy, keeping only its date, type, number, the role and the decision, deletes any driving licence copy, keeping the check results, and stops Update Service status checks.

Within 10 working days, the HR Manager closes the staff record: leaving date and reason, final pay and P45, property returned, and any open claim, investigation, allegation or referral, placing a retention hold where needed under the Records Management and Retention Policy.

At the same time the HR Manager deletes the emergency contact details and, once they are counted in the anonymised figures, the equality monitoring answers, creates the staff record summary and records the destruction date for each part of the record.

Records are then deleted through the quarterly retention review under the Records Management and Retention Policy. Deleting in CareFlow removes an item so that no user can open it, but CareFlow does not yet erase it permanently, so the HR Manager also asks the CareFlow supplier in writing to erase it; the same applies to applicant records, which CareFlow cannot yet delete.

blocks.p: A payslip, letter or email sent to the wrong person, a lost staff list, a colleague's details shown to someone not entitled to them, or payslips our payroll bureau sends to the wrong people is a personal data breach. Whoever finds it phones the office (the On-call Manager out of hours) at once and records it in the incident log before the end of their shift. The HR Manager is breach lead under the Personal Data Breach Procedure, which grades staff health, DBS and criminal offence information and bank details at severity 3 or higher and sets how the Nominated Individual decides on and makes any report to the Information Commission, within 72 hours of awareness where feasible as Article 33 requires. The HR Manager tells the staff affected.

blocks.p: Shortfalls go into the service improvement plan within 5 working days. Restricted information opened without a work reason is recorded in the incident log and handled under the Personal Data Breach Procedure and the Disciplinary Policy and Procedure.

The Registered Manager reviews this policy every 12 months with the HR Manager, and sooner after a change in data protection or employment law or guidance, a breach involving staff information, an inspection or audit finding, or when monitoring shows the arrangements are not working. The Directors approve it under the Policy Management and Document Control Policy.
